meta.title: FORGE — HYROX Training & Race-Prep Library (Full Gym + HYROX Station Equipment)
equipment_allowed: Treadmill / Indoor Track / Outdoor Run Route

Novice.station_load: Scaled loads (~60-70% of race-standard) until movement quality is solid under fatigue
Novice.conditioning_intensity: Zone 2 for all running; stations at controlled, technically clean pace — never race pace
Novice.rpe_cap: RPE 6-7 max on any single session
Novice.notes: Priority is owning the 8 station movement patterns and pacing an easy run before any fatigue is introduced. No compromised-running (station-then-run) work yet — build the run and the stations separately first.

Beginner.conditioning_intensity: Zone 2-3 running; stations introduced at race-pace effort for short segments
Beginner.rpe_cap: RPE 7 standard, RPE 8 on the one hard session/week
Beginner.notes: Introduce short compromised-running (run 400-800m directly off a station) at low volume — this is the single most HYROX-specific skill and the one general running/gym training does not build on its own.

Intermediate.station_load: Full race-standard load for your category
Intermediate.conditioning_intensity: Zone 3-4 running; race-pace station work becomes the default, not the exception
Intermediate.rpe_cap: RPE 7-8 standard, RPE 9 on brick/simulation sessions
Intermediate.notes: Brick sessions (station immediately into a timed run repeat) become a weekly staple. Pacing strategy — even split vs. controlled positive split — starts to matter as much as raw fitness.

Advanced.station_load: Full race-standard load, with periodized overload sessions above race weight
Advanced.conditioning_intensity: Zone 3-5 running; regular partial and full race simulations
Advanced.rpe_cap: RPE 8-9 standard, RPE 9-10 on simulation days
Advanced.notes: Individualize which 2-3 stations are the actual time-losers on your own race splits and bias extra volume there rather than treating all 8 stations as equal priority.

Elite.training_age: 6+ years / competing at Pro or World-Championship level
Elite.station_load: Full race-standard-or-heavier load, fully individualized to weak stations
Elite.conditioning_intensity: Autoregulated — written zones are a floor, not a target
Elite.notes: Total weekly training load is usually the thing to trim, not add, once technique and race-pacing are already sound — HYROX reward specificity and freshness over raw volume at this level.

Open / Singles.format: Solo athlete completes the full race alone: 8x 1km run + 8 stations (SkiErg 1000m, Sled Push 50m, Sled Pull 50m, Burpee Broad Jumps 80m, Row 1000m, Farmers Carry 200m, Sandbag Lunges 100m, Wall Balls 100 reps) in fixed alternating order.
Open / Singles.load_note: Standard Open-division loads for your competition age/gender category — confirm current official HYROX weight/rep standards before race day, as they are periodically updated.
Open / Singles.notes: Pacing the full 8-round alternation solo is the core skill — every session in this library, aside from short technique/power work, should reinforce running while fatigued from a station, not running fresh.

Doubles.format: Two athletes split all 8x 1km runs and all 8 stations between them, in whatever split ratio the pair agrees on station-by-station (station reps/distance are typically split, not duplicated).
Doubles.load_note: Same station loads as Open/Singles per HYROX Doubles rules — the advantage is splitting the work, not lighter weight.
Doubles.notes: Programming should include partner-coordinated sessions (alternating work/rest intervals matching your actual race split plan) in addition to individual training — a mismatched pacing strategy between partners costs more time than either partner's raw fitness.

Relay.format: Team of 4: each athlete runs 2x 1km and completes 2 of the 8 stations, once each.
Relay.load_note: Same per-station loads as Open/Singles, but each athlete only executes each station once — total individual volume is far lower.
Relay.notes: Because total per-athlete volume is short, training should bias toward higher-intensity, shorter-duration power work over aerobic base — a Relay leg rewards near-maximal output on 2 stations and 2km of running, not pacing management across 8 rounds.

Pro.format: Same solo 8x1km + 8-station format as Open/Singles, at the heavier Pro-division station loads.
Pro.load_note: Pro-division loads (heavier sled push/pull, sandbag, farmers carry, wall ball per current official HYROX Pro standards) — confirm current numbers, as Pro loading has been revised between seasons.
Pro.notes: Strength-to-weight ratio on the loaded stations (sled, farmers carry, sandbag) becomes a bigger limiter at Pro loads than in Open — dedicate more weekly volume to heavy strength work under this category than any other.

global_rules: Full commercial gym plus HYROX-specific station equipment (SkiErg, RowErg, sled + turf lane, farmers handles, sandbags, wall balls) is assumed on-site — no equipment constraint applies to any template in this library.

The single most HYROX-specific training skill is running while already fatigued from a station (‘compromised running’) — general running fitness and general station strength each transfer only partially on their own; brick/simulation sessions that combine them are what programs actually race performance.

Roxzone (station-entry and exit) transitions cost real race time — practice moving from the final run stride directly into the station's starting position, and from the station's last rep directly into a running stride, not just the work itself.

Pacing strategy is category-specific: Open/Singles and Pro reward an even or slightly negative split across all 8 rounds; Doubles rewards a pacing plan matched between both partners; Relay rewards near-maximal effort on a short, single exposure.
Deload every 4th week: cut running volume and station volume by ~40% at the same intensity, all levels.
Race-week taper (final block below) replaces normal training in the 7-10 days before a race — do not run a normal training week and a taper week back to back.

Confirm current official HYROX station distances, rep counts, and weight standards before race day — they are governed by HYROX and have been revised between seasons; treat the loads referenced in this library as a training-planning baseline, not a substitute for the official rulebook.

taper_progression.note: Final normal-ish session; volume already ~60% of a peak week.
Short sharpener + light station walkthrough; intensity stays crisp, volume drops further.

templates.notes_block: Run this in place of normal training for the 7-10 days before race day — do not stack this on top of a normal training week.
